examples.text: We wormed our way through the underbrush.

glosses: To move with one's body dragging the ground.

examples.text: Inch by inch I wormed along the secret passageway, flat to the ground, not once raising my head, hardly daring to pull a full breath[…].

glosses: To work one's way by artful or devious means.

examples.text: When debates and fretting jealousy / Did worm and work within you more and more, / Your colour faded.

glosses: To work (one's way or oneself) (into) gradually or slowly; to insinuate.

examples.text: He wormed his way into the organization.

With “facts” generated by Wikipedia worming themselves into every corner of our digital lives, such as your Alexa speaker or iPhone, perhaps it’s the ubiquity of information that’s the problem – and something that should concern us all.

glosses: To effect, remove, drive, draw, or the like, by slow and secret means.

examples.text: They […]find themselves wormed out of all power.

glosses: To drag out of, to get information that someone is reluctant or unwilling to give (through artful or devious means or by pleading or asking repeatedly).

examples.text: They[…]wormed things out of me that I had no desire to tell.

He nodded. "Mum's the word, Mrs. Bunting! It'll all be in the last editions of the evening newspapers—it can't be kep' out. There'd be too much of a row if twas!"
 "Are you going off to that public-house now?" she asked.
 "I've got a awk'ard job—to try and worm something out of the barmaid."

glosses: To fill in the contlines of (a rope) before parcelling and serving.

examples.text: Worm and parcel with the lay; turn and serve the other way.

glosses: To deworm (an animal).

examples.text: The men[…] assisted the laird in his sporting parties, wormed his dogs, and cut the ears of his terrier puppies.

glosses: To clean by means of a worm; to draw a wad or cartridge from, as a firearm.
